title: Planetary Multi-Master Database with Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC)
subtitle: Spanner-like Linearizability, Clock Scew Bounding and Multi-Region Active-Active Consensus
problem_statement: A multi-region active-active database deployed across US, Europe, and Asia allows local concurrent writes. Due to NTP clock drift between AWS regions (exceeding 80ms), Last-Write-Wins (LWW) conflict resolution causes newer financial transactions to be overwritten by older transactions, violating causal consistency.

faded_bug.description: Physical time step drift without max-skew bound checking permits unbounded logical clock inflation.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff: + if abs(msgPhysical - now) > MAX_CLOCK_OFFSET_MS { panic("NTP clock skew exceeded safety threshold") }

invariants.description: Causal ordering must be preserved: if event A causes event B, HLC(A) < HLC(B) globally.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the difference between Google Spanner's TrueTime API (using atomic clocks and GPS) and CockroachDB's Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC).
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If two nodes in US and EU have a physical clock skew of 200ms, how does the uncertainty interval `[t.earliest, t.latest]` ensure serializability during read-only transactions?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: An NTP daemon on node EU goes rogue and reports a timestamp 10 years in the future. How do HLC consensus protocols prevent the entire cluster clock from jumping forward?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Cross-region consensus requires WAN round-trips (70ms US-EU). How do Multi-Raft leaseholders enable single-region 2ms reads without cross-region coordinator communication?

counter_probes.counter_question: NTP over commodity internet routinely experiences 50ms to 250ms of jitter and asymmetric network routes. Can standard NTP guarantee linearizable ordering in a multi-master distributed DB?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: No. Commodity NTP cannot guarantee bounded error. A multi-master DB requires TrueTime hardware uncertainty bounds or HLC (Hybrid Logical Clocks) with strict maximum offset abort thresholds.
